text.text_excerpt: Kolache Kitchen is a cute spot on Freret St serving Kolaches (among many many other things!). Right now during Covid, there is a max limit of 5 customers inside the building at once, so be mindful that you might have to stand outside for just a bit. Masks are required. I always appreciate this dedication to employee and customer safety! For the food: I got the cream cheese kolache and a frozen Vietnamese coffee. My partner got the BBQ brisket sandwich. We both loved these menu items. I will say, as a vegetarian my menu options at Kolache Kitchen, especially in the savory foods department, are pretty limited (but I have a huge sweet tooth so it's not a huge issue). I LOVE KOLACHE KITCHEN. It's honestly pretty exciting to finally have them outside of Freret St. and to have access to them in the CBD area. The staff here is so friendly. This location is a little bit smaller than their first location in New Orleans, but they have a community table with stools to eat right quick. Food is superb and I'm just so happy my kolache obsession continues getting fed. Just know they don't have a soda fountain but the star of the show is their food menu so I highly recommend supporting them and checking them out.

I absolutely love the Kolache kitchen. I was first introduced to this establishment in Baton Rouge while attending college, I was immediately hooked. Now living in New Orleans I'm so excited that we have two locations! This location is right by my job in the CBD and however you can certainly miss it if you're using gps. I passed it up twice because the signage is kind of small but it's worth the hassle of trying to find. I ordered the Patton sausage and bacon Kolache. The Patton sausage Kolache was outstanding, I absolutely loved it! The bread is soft, sweet, warm and outright sinful. It was stuffed with meat and the prices are super reasonable!
